- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md: lines 1, 26-35, 100-106, 123-130 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The LAST RUN DIFF claims to synchronize the root audit-plans.md with its template counterpart, but the root file on disk at lines 1 and 102-103 still shows the OLD text ("/implement-plan-claude projects" not "legacy /implement-plan-claude projects", and "/implement-plan-claude (in-session) or /implement-plan-ai (AI orchestrator)" instead of "Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off / default-engine hand-off"). The template at workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md:1 has the updated text.
  WHY: The /audit-plans command in the session will describe /implement-plan-claude as an in-session implementer rather than a Claude-engine orchestrator hand-off, misleading the user. The conflict screen will look for in-session projects instead of legacy projects.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 267-270 (_shell_segments_with_operators redirect handling, already present in the template before this PR) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The parser unconditionally pops a trailing numeric token before a redirect operator without checking whether the digit is adjacent to the operator. A shell command git push origin 2 > /dev/null where 2 is a quoted branch name produces tokens [git, push, origin, 2, >, /dev/null] after shlex strips quotes; the parser drops 2, sees no refspec, and falls back to checking the current branch instead of branch 2. In bash the same command also consumes 2 as a file-descriptor specifier, making the parser behavior consistent with the shell, but the guard cannot detect the push-target intent when the branch name is a digit and the command also includes a redirect.
  WHY: An interactive session that genuinely pushes to a branch whose name is a single digit (e.g. git push origin 1) while also redirecting output would have the guard check the wrong branch. In practice this requires an extremely contrived command shape and the guard already falls back to checking the current branch, which is the safe default.
